subject: Community Compact Agreement Signing
overview: Mayor Stephanie Muccini Burke and Lieutenant Governor Karyn Polito signed a Community Compact agreement establishing best practices for financial accountability, transportation, and economic development. The partnership secures technical assistance and grant funding to support citywide mobility and the revitalization of Medford Square.

items.title: Introduction and Financial Accountability Compact
items.summary: Mayor Burke announced the city's commitment to a financial accountability compact aimed at streamlining disparate software systems into a single, transparent open-checkbook system.

items.title: Complete Streets Initiative
items.summary: City Engineer Cassandra Koutalidis detailed plans to improve roadway connectivity and safety for pedestrians, cyclists, and transit users of all abilities through a new prioritization plan.

items.title: Medford Square Revitalization and Economic Development
items.summary: Director Lauren DiLorenzo announced a $40,000 planning grant from the MAPC to develop an economic strategy for Medford Square focused on retail diversity, housing, and riverfront access.

items.title: Remarks from the State Delegation
items.summary: Representative Christine Barber spoke on the importance of state and local collaboration to address government transparency and community mobility.

items.title: Lieutenant Governor's Address on Municipal Partnerships
items.summary: Lieutenant Governor Polito explained that Medford is the 156th community to join the voluntary program, which grants the city preferential scoring for infrastructure and MassWorks grants.

items.title: Municipal Modernization and Official Signing
items.summary: The Mayor and Lieutenant Governor signed the formal Community Compact agreement following a brief discussion on the state's Municipal Modernization Bill.
